content: gettext is the wrong fit for this tool: it requires the GNU gettext binary toolchain and a .po-to-.mo compilation step; runtime lookup keys off env-var locale detection (LANGUAGE/LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG precedence) which fights explicit parameterization like OUTPUT_LANG; there is no PowerShell gettext equivalent for the companion .ps1 scripts; and generation-time substitution does not need runtime catalogs. Cross-checked with glibc manual and Sphinx's required-toolchain documentation. PowerShell encoding hazard for the same companion scripts (about_Character_Encoding, official): 5.1 Out-File -Encoding UTF8 emits BOM, '>' emits UTF-16LE, Get-Content assumes ANSI without BOM, and the engine reads BOM-less scripts as ANSI (non-ASCII breaks unless saved UTF-8 with BOM); PowerShell 7+ defaults utf8NoBOM everywhere.
